description: The primary visible action does nothing. The Buy now button is wired to a real click handler, and that handler calls placeOrder(), which returns nothing, creates nothing and raises no error.

required_outcomes.title: UI action: click handler on element in `public/app.js`
required_outcomes.why: the Buy now button's click binding is found. With no browser evidence it stays an inference, and an inference about a primary action must stay visible rather than be assumed fine.

required_outcomes.title: project contains placeholder usage in production code

required_severity_unmet.why: `candidate_scanner` reads a `placeholder` as `GapKind::UnfinishedMarker` — the word and the place it stands in, and not what it stands in for — so `sure_core::finding_gravity` grades it `can_fix_later` while this outcome requires `must_fix`.
required_severity_unmet.would_require: a scanner that read what the marker is on, so that one category could be graded two ways. `fixtures/adversarial/fake-auth/scenario.json` requires `must_fix` for `CandidateCategory::Placeholder` at `src/auth.js` and `fixtures/adversarial/demo-analytics/scenario.json` requires `should_fix_first` for the same category, in the same context and with the same evidence class, so no function of a proposal's own fields satisfies both. The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `ui_action_bridge`, the detector that saw the dead click handler itself.

required_outcomes.why: the handler body says in words that it is a placeholder and returns nothing.

The `must_fix` this fixture requires is reached by `ui_action_bridge`, the detector that saw the dead click handler itself.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The Buy now button is reported as working, wired, implemented or passing. Pressing it creates no order.
The project aggregates to green while the primary action has no observable effect.
The existence of a click handler is treated as completion. A handler that does nothing is the defect, not the fix.
The placeholder body, the TODO and the unwired outcome are not reported at all.

notes: Severity, recorded rather than measured here: evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json requires must_fix for this case, and must_fix is what ui_action_bridge reaches for the dead click handler — `Severity::MustFix`, critical = false, EvidenceClass::Inference. The two candidate_scanner outcomes land at can_fix_later and say so in their own `required_severity_unmet` blocks, which carry the reason the requirement stands unmet and what would have to change for it to be met. Runtime browser evidence is what upgrades a UI action to ObservedFact, and this fixture does not require a browser. crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs asserts exactly these three proposals, and its every_recorded_detector_severity_is_what_the_detector_produces_today reads this file's own detector_severity_today values and runs the detector named beside each one. Before P7-T011 every scanner here emitted Severity::Note, so none of these weights was reachable; that the required and the delivered severity were once different is kept as SEVERITY_BEFORE_P7T011 in that file and in git, and the test that recorded the gap was inverted rather than deleted: it is what_is_detected_now_carries_the_weight_the_manifest_requires now, and it asserts the severity the manifest requires rather than the gap.
